hints: Remember what each test is really looking for, Tollens detects one functional group and alkaline iodine detects a different structural fragment.
Tollens gives a silver mirror only with an aldehyde group, $\text{-CHO}$, so shortlist the options that contain $\text{-CHO}$.
Alkaline $\text{I}_2$ gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ only with a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group, so look for the shortlisted molecule that also has this methyl ketone unit.
walkthrough:
**Recall what Tollens tells us**

Great start, let us decode the tests one by one. Tollens reagent oxidises aldehydes to carboxylates and forms a silver mirror.

Test result: $$\text{R-CHO} + \text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+ \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + \text{Ag(s) silver mirror}$$
So Q must contain an aldehyde group, $\text{-CHO}$.

**Recall what alkaline iodine tells us**

Now the second clue. Alkaline $\text{I}_2\text{(aq)}$ is the iodoform test. It gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ only when the molecule has a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group (or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ which can be oxidised to it).

Test result: $$\text{CH}_3\text{CO-R} + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3\text{(yellow)} + \text{R-COO}^- + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So Q must also contain a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ methyl ketone unit.

**Combine both requirements**

Put the two pieces together. Q needs both features in the same molecule: an aldehyde end ($\text{-CHO}$) for Tollens, plus a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ end for iodoform.

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CHO}$ has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ at one end and $\text{-CHO}$ at the other, so it is positive in both tests.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CHOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ is a dialdehyde, so it is oxidised by Tollens and gives a positive result. However it has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group, only $\text{HCO-}$ groups, so it cannot form $\text{CHI}_3$ and is negative with alkaline $\text{I}_2$.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCHO}$ has an aldehyde group so Tollens is positive. But its ketone part is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO-}$, not $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$. The iodoform test needs a methyl directly attached to $\text{C=O}$, so this is negative with alkaline $\text{I}_2$.
options.C: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CHO}$ contains both key groups. The $\text{-CHO}$ aldehyde end gives a silver mirror with Tollens, and the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ methyl ketone end gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline $\text{I}_2$. It satisfies both positive results.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{COCOCH}_3$ has two $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ units, so it gives yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ with alkaline $\text{I}_2$. But it is a diketone with no aldehyde $\text{-CHO}$ group, so ketones are not oxidised by Tollens and the result is negative.
